policies.name: AiCostSpike
policies.summary: AI spend is three times yesterday's rate
policies.description: Cost per request is a success metric in its own right. A spike is usually abuse, a retry loop, or a prompt that grew.

policies.name: AvailabilityBudgetBurnFast
policies.summary: Burning the availability budget 14.4x faster than sustainable
policies.description: At this rate the entire 30-day error budget is gone in about two days. Check which revision is serving; if a release is in flight, shift traffic back to the previous one.

policies.name: AvailabilityBudgetBurnMedium
policies.summary: Burning the availability budget 6x faster than sustainable
policies.description: Slower than a hard outage and easy to miss, but the budget is gone in about five days if it continues.

policies.name: AvailabilityBudgetBurnSlow
policies.summary: Availability budget burning 3x faster than sustainable
policies.description: Raise a ticket. This does not need waking anyone.

policies.name: AvailabilityBudgetBurnVerySlow
policies.summary: Availability budget will not last the window
policies.description: Spending faster than the budget replenishes. Nothing is broken right now, but the month ends out of budget unless this changes.

policies.name: AvailabilityBudgetExhausted
policies.description: Per the policy in docs/slo.md, feature releases pause and the next work is reliability until the window recovers.

policies.name: LatencyBudgetBurnFast
policies.summary: Burning the latency budget 14.4x faster than sustainable
policies.description: Compare rag_retrieval_duration_seconds against rag_answer_duration_seconds to see whether the vector search or the model is responsible, then open a trace for a slow request.

policies.name: LatencyBudgetBurnSlow
policies.summary: Latency budget burning 3x faster than sustainable
policies.description: Raise a ticket. Likely a gradual regression, not an incident.

policies.name: RetrievalQualityDrop
policies.summary: More than 20 percent of queries retrieve nothing
policies.description: Every request still succeeds, so no SLO notices. Either the index is stale or the questions being asked have drifted away from the corpus. Check the last successful indexer run.
